solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

Q085-01.notes: (x-3)(x+2-k)=0 gives roots 3 and k-2; exactly one solution when k-2=3, k=5 (double root). Trap: dividing by (x-3) loses x=3.

flags: minor: formula is given, so this is just solving n(n-1)=156; guess-and-check or graphing is immediate

Q085-03.notes: Legs along axes: x/10+y/8=1, area xy=8x(1-x/10) maximized at x=5, y=4 -> 20 (half the triangle's area).

flags: minor: the condition x != 2y explicitly eliminates choice C, leaving 3 as the only factor-root among the choices; -3 and 1/3 are sign/reciprocal distractors

Q085-07.notes: Semicircle areas: AB r=6 -> 18pi; AC r=2 -> 2pi; CB r=4 -> 8pi. 18-2-8=8pi. Distractor 10pi (subtract only one), 16pi/32pi (full circles).

flags: minor: requires interior-angle formula for regular polygons ((n-2)180/n); in scope but at the edge of commonly tested SAT geometry
minor: closely resembles a common released-SAT pattern (similar right triangles, find trig ratio of corresponding angle, 7-24-25 type triple)
Q085-10.notes: PQ=25. T corresponds to Q; cos Q=QR/PQ=7/25. Distractors: tan, sin, cot of Q.

Q085-11.notes: Corner triangles congruent (AE=BF=6). EF=10, so EB=sqrt(100-36)=8, side=6+8=14. 10sqrt2 is the 45-degree-rotation distractor; configuration is unique.

Q085-12.notes: Right angle at (1,2), so hypotenuse from (13,2) to (1,7) is a diameter: sqrt(144+25)=13, r=6.5. Trap: answering 13.

flags: minor: relies on a two-stage similar-triangle argument (or harmonic-mean result 2ab/(a+b)); in domain but at the upper limit of SAT difficulty
Q085-13.notes: AP/PC=15/10, so segment from P to AD = 10*15/25=6 on each side; total 12 = 2*15*10/25.

flags: minor: initial angle (sin x=8/17, about 28 degrees, base 15 ft from wall) is an unrealistically shallow, unsafe ladder angle
Q085-14.notes: Initially height=17*8/17=8. After, base=8 so height=15. Difference 7.
